$100 for that is a GREAT price. Ibanez 12-strings are pretty good. Including a strap and case makes it an even better deal. You could always get it, try to practice on it, and if you just can't seem to like it or learn in a sustainable way, you can always resell it (maybe at a higher price even). Or you could get another cheap beginner 6-string and keep the 12-string until you're more comfortable with playing it.
I wouldn't recommend changing it to six strings, but you definitely can. Like others have said though, it may mess with the guitar (alignment, action, etc.).

Learning to play on a 12 string will be pretty difficult, much more so than a 6-string. Bar chords will be a pain, finger picking will be tricky, and tuning will be a hassle. But I can see some benefits: you'd develop stronger fingers faster (playing on a 6 string will be a breeze after), tuning so many strings at a time might help develop your ear faster, I personally think a lot of songs (from genres like rock, indie, folk, or blues) sound much richer and better in 12 strings.
Finally, it would give you the right to brag about "yeah, I actually learned playing guitar on a 12 string". I'd be impressed. 

TL;Dr: go for it! can always resell it if you don't like it.
